newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares gains on pre-weekend dlr cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares gains on pre-weekend dlr cover.

text.p: The Mexican peso reined in earlier gains at the close Friday due to local dealers buying dollars to cover positions ahead of the weekend, traders said.
"The peso opened very strong, but relinquished strength when the same dealers selling dollars began to buy them back to cover positions prior to the weekend," a trader said.
The benchmark 48- and 24-hour pesos closed 0.9 and 0.2 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.5270/7.5320 and 7.5240/7.5280 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed 0.1 of a centavo firmer at 7.5115/7.5150 per dollar.
Traders said that the market decided to close dollar positions ahead of municipal elections Sunday in the state of Guerrero, which has recently been the scene of guerrilla activity.
"Although the market no longer pays much attention to these sorts of events, it is best to settle positions as a precaution," a trader said.
Few foreign investors traded during the session, even though they had been expected to step in after U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yields had fallen to below 6.75 percent to 6.74 percent.
For the week as a whole, the 48-hour peso closed 1.2 centavos firmer, compared to last Friday's close of 7.5400/7.5440.
